description: Sabotages for the observer's information queries (M16). Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format.
notCoveredHere: Sabotages of M16.1-M16.5 were run by hand when those items landed and were not recorded; they are not reconstructed here. The two administrative-share tests are #[ignore]d, so the sweep does not run them: the SMB2 and loopback entries below are caught by the pure conversion tests alone.

sabotages.name: basic info swaps the access and write times
sabotages.why: Both fields are FileTimes from the same structure, so the swap type-checks; only a test with distinct values per field can tell them apart.

sabotages.name: basic info drops the attributes
sabotages.why: A zero attribute word is a plausible answer for an ordinary file, so a test of a new file alone would pass; the directory and read-only tests need the bits.

sabotages.name: the 1601 epoch is off by a day
sabotages.why: The conversion tests check against literal dates rather than the constant, so a wrong constant cannot agree with itself.

sabotages.name: a tick is read as a microsecond
sabotages.why: Only the sub-second part uses the unit, so this survives every whole-second test and is caught by the 1-tick and 1.5-second cases.

sabotages.name: control: a negative count is cast rather than refused
sabotages.why: An equivalent mutant on Windows, measured: a negative count cast to unsigned is 2^63 ticks or more, which overflows SystemTime in the checked_add, so the answer is still None. The explicit refusal is kept so the contract does not rest on SystemTime's range; the comment at the site says so.

sabotages.name: control: the sub-second nanoseconds are cast rather than checked
sabotages.why: The remainder is below a second's ticks, so times 100 it is below 1e9 and always fits a u32; the checked conversion can never fail. A test that catches this is asserting the implementation.

sabotages.name: any protocol carries an SMB2 block
sabotages.why: The union member is defined only for SMB; reading it for another protocol reports capabilities that mean nothing.

sabotages.name: loopback reads the offline bit
sabotages.why: Each documented flag must be read from its own bit; the flag test sets each alone.

sabotages.name: the query buffer loses its 8-byte alignment
sabotages.why: Measured: FileRemoteProtocolInfo refuses a buffer aligned to 4 but not 8. No test catches the loss at run time, because a stack buffer usually lands 8-aligned anyway, so the const assertion is the guard.

sabotages.name: the buffer fill can be held in place by a callee
sabotages.why: A callee answering 'too small' with the size it was given would make the loop retry at the same size forever. Caught by assertion, not a hang: the stand-in answers once that way, and the test checks the retry was given a larger buffer.

sabotages.name: the buffer fill grows by less than the size reported
sabotages.why: Still converges, one unit at a time, so every result is right; only the recorded capacities show the extra calls.

sabotages.name: a full buffer is taken as a fit
sabotages.why: A return equal to the capacity is a size request, not a length: taking it as a length publishes a unit the callee never wrote and leaves no room for the terminator.

sabotages.name: a failure loses its error code
sabotages.why: The caller's only way to tell a device without a path from any other failure is the Win32 code.

sabotages.name: opened names are normalized
sabotages.why: Opened and Normalized were measured to differ only for an open by 8.3 short name and for a named pipe; the pipe test catches this wherever named pipes exist, the short-name test only where the volume has short names.

sabotages.name: the GUID form asks for the NT name
sabotages.why: Each volume form is checked against its own prefix, so a crossed flag shows as the wrong prefix.

sabotages.name: final_path names the volume by its NT device
sabotages.why: The default is the drive-letter form a caller can open again; the rename and move tests compare it with the canonical path.

sabotages.name: a volume name keeps its NUL padding
sabotages.why: The call reports no lengths, only terminated names in zeroed buffers; without the cut each name is MAX_PATH + 1 units, mostly NULs.

sabotages.name: a name with no NUL is read as empty
sabotages.why: A name filling the whole buffer has no terminator; it is the whole buffer, not nothing.

sabotages.name: the serial number and component length are crossed
sabotages.why: Both are u32 out-parameters next to each other, so the swap type-checks; the comparison with the root-path query sees it.

sabotages.name: the flags are dropped
sabotages.why: No flags is a legal answer, so only a comparison with what the volume reports by another route can tell.

sabotages.name: the sparse-files flag has the wrong bit
sabotages.why: Every named value is checked against windows-sys' constant of the same name, and separately against the volume's own answer to FSCTL_SET_SPARSE.
find: pub const SUPPORTS_SPARSE_FILES: Self = Self { bits: 0x0000_0040 };
replace: pub const SUPPORTS_SPARSE_FILES: Self = Self { bits: 0x0000_0080 };

sabotages.name: contains accepts any shared bit
sabotages.why: 'Has every one of these' and 'has one of these' agree for a single flag, so only a multi-bit query separates them.

sabotages.name: or intersects
sabotages.why: Combining two distinct flags with & gives no flags at all.

sabotages.name: control: the name buffers are twice the documented size
sabotages.why: MAX_PATH + 1 is the documented maximum; a larger buffer only leaves more unused space. A test that catches this is asserting the buffer size, not the answer.
find: const NAME_UNITS: usize = MAX_PATH as usize + 1;

sabotages.name: the volume query cancels the handle's I/O
sabotages.why: M16.10's claim is that EVERY query leaves a pending operation alone, and the M15.5 tests already cover file_len's path. This patch breaks a query only the shared table issues while an operation pends, so the pending connect and read are aborted rather than completed.

sabotages.name: the final-path query cancels the handle's I/O
sabotages.why: As the volume entry, for a query on a different call path: GetFinalPathNameByHandleW rather than GetVolumeInformationByHandleW or GetFileInformationByHandleEx.
